transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. I'm here because I have an overwhelming, intense fear of dogs that has become too difficult for me to manage. It is really starting to disrupt my life, and I'm hoping to get some help with it.
Can you describe what happens when you encounter a dog or even think about one? For example, do you feel panic, avoid certain places, or have physical symptoms?

Just thinking about running into a dog makes me incredibly anxious, so I actively avoid parks or walking down certain streets. If I actually see one, I panic immediately—my heart starts racing, I sweat, and I feel like I can't breathe.
How long have you experienced this fear of dogs, and has it been consistently affecting your daily activities for at least six months or more?

Yes, I've had this intense fear of dogs for about a year and nine months now. It has consistently affected my daily life and activities for that entire time, especially since I have to constantly change my routes to avoid them.
